content:
28th November
It's nearly December. In fact, it will be next week. How do you feel about that? I'm undecided and I also have cold feet. But enough of that, welcome back to our regular feature where we say a bit about the games we've been playing this week! This week, Bertie has been enjoying Leonida but also rural England in the 17th century; Connor has been being a total scumbag and has also found himself coincidentally imprisoned; Matt keeps having revelations and can't stop discovering new things; and Dom's getting dirty looks. Again.
But forget about us, what about you? What have you been playing this week? Let us know below. And don't forget that we have an entire archive of previous What We've Been Playings for your perusal should you want to know what you were playing week, month, or even a year ago.
GTA 6 / Hunter's Moon, PS5
I've mostly been playing GTA 6 and I really like it. What I've been most surprised by is the game's maturity, which seems like an odd thing to say when people are having things rammed up their wotsits, and there's so much deliberately stupid and slapstick stuff happening. But there's another level that exists primarily between Jason and Lucia. It's evident in moments such as helping Lucia build flatpack furniture, then watching a montage of tender moments around that flatpack furniture, which looked a lot like life, like actual life, to me. Two people doing life together, existing, overlapping. I don't know that we've ever seen a relationship in so much detail before. It's really impressive.
I also admired the many ways Rockstar never loses sight of this being a game, despite the many added layers of realism. You can feel it in the way the game allows a buffer before reacting to you; you can knock a few street posts over before anyone cares, stop traffic as much as you like. It's even more evident in missions when the game teleports you somewhere to cut out the journey, because that's more fun. I did a mission yesterday where the whole city lit up like a club, pulsing to the music; that wasn't realism but it sure as hell was fun.
But I also wanted to give a shout-out to a game called Hunter's Moon. It's an indie sort of walking sim released around Halloween, appropriately, because it revolves around the topic of witch hunting in England back in the 17th century. You find yourself - you don't really know who you are - on the run through nighttime rural England as you try and seek shelter from pursuing witch hunters. As you do, you encounter houses and vignettes that play out in window frames there, which pull you deeper into this fearful period of time. They're nicely acted moments; what a difference it makes when actors record their lines together, rather than have them recorded individually and stitched together later on.
I don't know that it's strong enough to recommend unless you have a powerful interest in this subject matter - it's a bit flat and one-note - but it's effective at placing you into a misconstrued area such that you can feel the fear of someone persecuted for no reasonable reason.
-Bertie
GTA 6, PS5; World of Warcraft: Forever, PC
I've been trying to see how GTA 6 reacts to me being a total scumbag and I've not been left disappointed. The game made me feel pretty awful for kicking a dog like five times which is a sign I've not become a heartless monster. In my defence, they were let loose on me by some drug dealer, but given I can't prove the dog itself was slinging snow, my actions still haunt me.
When not making my way through GTA 6 I've been locked into the World of Warcraft: Forever prison and continue to love my bars and cold stone walls. This week I intend to get my fishing level up to 300 and take on the Stranglethorn Fishing Extravaganza. As additional preparation, I'm opening the same four lobster cages off the shore of Desolace in hopes of getting a better rod. MMO's man, they're the best. Shout out to Blizzard for giving Balance Druids a massive buff yesterday. Kisses.
-Connor
Queen's Domain, PC
Last time I excitedly chattered about Queen's Domain here, I was, I think, about five hours in. It already had the suggestion of something really special, even back then. But little did I know what else was in store. Some 40 or so hours later, it's easily one of my favourite games this year: an extraordinary first-person action-RPG that (as I said in my effusive five-star Queen's Domain review) has echoes of a lot of things - King's Field, Dark Souls, Zelda, even a touch of Metroidvania - but still manages to feel entirely its own. Its world is one of secrets upon secrets upon secrets, to the point that, even after seeing an ending or two, I'm still plugging away. Last night, I had a bit of a revelation, propelling me still further into its tangled web of mysteries; to places and encounters that still managed to surprise. What an absolute gem.
-Matt
The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+, Switch 2
It is 2011, and I am getting dirty looks in public for playing the original, vanilla, naked The Binding of Isaac in public on my crappy little gaming laptop I brought off a friend for a pack of beers and some homemade bread. It is 2014, and a woman on a bus calls me 'disgusting' and 'a charlatan' because I am playing The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth on my PlayStation Vita, in a posh little district of Bournemouth where the average resident is over 70 years old. It is 2021, and a doctor looks at me with deep, deep concern because I'm recovering from an operation and playing The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth on my Nintendo Switch in the hospital. It is 2026, and some of the friends I've made in my yoga classes give me a look of regrettable disdain because they see me sitting in a cafe playing The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ on my Switch 2 after a particularly sweaty vinyasa class. I've been living with the public's disapproval for my taste in roguelikes for 15 years now, and if that hasn't stopped me crying tears of blood at a massive poop in my mother's basement yet, nothing will.
-Dom
